headline: How to read your bone age
DNR this slide
body: Educational and research purposes only. Not medical advice. Two published studies, every number quoted from the paper.

headline: Bone age
body: Bone age is read from a hand and wrist X-ray. That one number then gets used to estimate remaining growth for your whole skeleton. | The problem is the hand is on its own schedule and it is the first thing to finish, so reading your legs off it is not to our benefit.
punch: Your hand is not where your height comes from.

headline: Fusion order
body: Mice: *epiphyseal fusion* at **3 weeks** phalanges, **4 weeks** metacarpals, tibia and femur still open at **12 weeks**. | Rats: **12 weeks** phalanges, **16 weeks** metacarpals, legs still open at 16. Same order both species.

headline: Growth rate
body: At one week: metacarpal growth rate **49%** of tibial. *Proliferation per column* **46%**. | Every marker of *growth plate senescence* (the plate running out of divisions) more advanced in the hand bones at the same age. So the hand is slower and older the whole way.

headline: The pathway
body: *Chondrocytes* from finger bones divide slower than leg bone chondrocytes. Add IGF-1 to the finger cells: proliferation rose **to match untreated leg cells**. | My takeaway is the cells are the same, the hand just gets less signal. That is the pathway behind the whole difference.
punch: The bone is the same. The signal is not.

headline: Human data
body: MRI, **958 people**, 14 to 21, wrist knee and ankle. Fusion varied by site inside one person. Complete fusion about **2 years earlier** in girls. | *Pubertal stage* correlated with fusion at every site, **0.514 to 0.598** in males. Our best marker to track is puberty stage, not age.

headline: Training vs BMI
body: **BMI** correlated with plate maturity, 0.186 to 0.384. **Physical activity**: no significant correlation in males at any site, one very low correlation at the female wrist (**0.095**), nothing else. | So training is not what is spending your plates. Body composition tracked it.

headline: Today's takeaway
body: Read bone age as an estimate from your fastest ageing bones, not your legs. Track pubertal stage. The hand finishes first, always. | Tomorrow: part 2.
